text:
alex: Heads up — canary rollout for release `r2026-03` shows a sustained ~25% token/sec drop on continuous-batcher paths starting at ~09:12 UTC. Queues look healthy but queue-to-dispatch deadtime is high.

infra-bot: alert: canary-1 latency spike detected (token/sec -24%, p99 latency +40ms) — triggered at 09:14 UTC

sam: oof. did we change kernel selection heuristics in that release?

alex: yes — there was a change that prefers the 'small-cpy' memcpy kernel when batch_size < 8 during kernel selection pass. commit: abcdef1 (merged yesterday).

maria: I ran a short perf sample on a reproducer. hotspots: ``memcpy_small_kernel`` and ``kv_cache_lookup``. memcpy_small_kernel is ~42% of CPU in CTB workers, previously it was ~12%.

alex: can you paste the perf flame lines?

maria: pasted minimal output:
```
  42.1%  worker  [.] memcpy_small_kernel
  21.3%  worker  [.] kernel_select_path
  11.8%  worker  [.] kv_cache_lookup
  6.4%   worker  [.] schedule_batch
```

sam: interesting — kernel_select_path jumps because for tiny batches we changed the path that selects a memcpy variant that avoids vectorized memcpy, but on our hardware that scalar path thrashes L1 and causes pipeline stalls. That would increase deadtime between enqueue and dispatch.

ops-jen: CI perf job `perf/ctb-throughput` also flagged this — job 6789: baseline 1825 tok/s, head 1360 tok/s, regression ~25%. Link: https://ci.internal/job/6789

alex: ok bisect plan: revert abcdef1 in a canary build, run canary-1 perf harness and a 10min CTB soak. If that restores tok/s we gate the revert.

maria: reproduced locally with small-replay fixture (short sequences, batch <8): toggling that memcpy path flips tok/s from 1400 -> 1850. I can produce perf traces for both.

sam: other option: tweak heuristic threshold from 8 -> 4 to reduce scalar memcpy usage. Might be less risky than full revert. But if kernel selection has other downstream effects, revert is safer.

alex: can we get a quick microbenchmark of memcpy variants on our instance types? if scalar variant is slower across the board we should just revert. Maria — can you run memcpy_bench with lengths 32..1024 across kernels?

maria: running now, results ETA 8m.

ci-bot: perf/ctb-throughput #6790 started (compare r2026-03 HEAD vs revert-abcdef1)

(8m later)

maria: bench summary: for 32..256 bytes: scalar memcpy (small-cpy) is ~1.4x slower than vector memcpy on our Ampere gen. For >512 bytes differences narrow. Full numeric csv attached to the job.

sam: that matches the perf flame. The heuristic was well-intentioned (reduce memory bandwidth for tiny payloads) but on our target GPU-CPU node the scalar path is worse due to missed block-copy optimizations.

alex: rolling revert to canary-1 now (deploy revert-abcdef1). I'll watch token/sec and p99.

infra-bot: deploy canary-1 revert-abcdef1 started at 09:38 UTC

(6m later)

infra-bot: deploy canary-1 revert-abcdef1 completed at 09:44 UTC

alex: initial numbers — tok/s back up to ~1860, p99 down to baseline. Looks like revert fixed it.

ci-bot: perf/ctb-throughput #6790 finished: head (revert) = 1848 tok/s, base = 1825 tok/s, delta +1.3% (no regression)

sam: great. next steps: open a PR to revert abcdef1 with a clear note about memcpy variant perf on Ampere nodes and add a microbenchmark CI gate for memcpy heuristics. We can rework heuristic to consult a node-capability table instead of a blanket threshold.

maria: I'll attach the perf traces and bench CSV to the revert PR. Also adding a short test in the perf suite that runs memcpy_bench on instance flavor matrix.

alex: thanks all. Filing a postmortem/short blameless note in incidents channel.

ops-jen: left a runbook update to avoid rolling kernel-selection changes without perf microbenchmarks. :thumbsup:

sam: leaving a follow-up todo: audit other heuristics that pick micro-kernels based on batch size only — we should prefer runtime shape+hw lookup.

alex: good discussion. closing this thread once PR merges.
